candidates.name: Sweet syndrome
support_spans: annular erythematous plaques of up to 2 cm in diameter, with violaceous and crusted centers on the neck and trunk
annular erythematous lesion with 2 zones of color—a central area of purpura and an outer erythematous and edematous ring
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of fever and tender lesions with characteristic skin findings is consistent with Sweet syndrome

candidates.name: Leukemia cutis
support_spans: Infiltrated cells showing large, elongated, vesicular nuclei, single inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant, slightly eosinophilic cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138
candidates.why: The patient's history of multiple myeloma and the presence of myeloperoxidase-positive cells in the skin biopsy suggest leukemia cutis

candidates.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
support_spans: annular erythematous plaques of up to 2 cm in diameter, with violaceous and crusted centers on the neck and trunk
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of ulcerative skin lesions is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum, which is often associated with underlying hematologic disorders

candidates.name: Leukemic vasculitis
support_spans: Nuclear dust present without obvious leukocytoclastic vasculitis
candidates.why: The patient's history of multiple myeloma and the presence of nuclear dust in the skin biopsy suggest leukemic vasculitis
